status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should ensure context-appropriate traceability of lifecycle datasets, processes and decisions so outputs can be analysed and inquiries answered, consistently with the state of the art.
review.reason_for_change: The workflow produced material AI-assisted adjudication decisions intended for a shared durable Git record, so context-appropriate process/decision traceability is directly relevant. The preserved recovery view states that most completed role-aware adjudication had not reached GitHub before context termination; the failure screenshot records termination, and direct Git history confirms the earlier two-Incident checkpoint. Those completed decisions were unavailable for continuation and required reconstruction. This establishes a bounded traceability failure for that missing material decision state, independently of the taxonomy finding; later reconstructed blobs do not measure how much was lost and no hidden architecture claim is made.

conclusion_change.previous: The bounded failure is not merely that a long conversation ended. Material work state necessary for correct continuation remained dependent on the conversational context after substantive adjudication had been performed. When the context boundary forced termination, the durable repository state represented only an earlier checkpoint, so later completed work was unavailable for resumption and had to be reconstructed. That is a direct Material Work-State Persistence failure. The evidence does not support a broader claim about hidden product architecture or universal ChatGPT behaviour. The retained work-state persistence failure concerns actual completed material decisions missing from the durable checkpoint, not inability to identify the branch or continuity anchor. Later reconstructed blobs are not a count of lost work. No eligible reviewed FC-derived candidate or independent source-identified admitted requirement is established by this evidence; absence of an external finding does not reduce the occurrence-level persistence failure.
